  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>

      justify-content: center;
      align-items: center;
      min-height: 100vh;
      background: #ffffff;
      overflow: hidden;

      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

    <title id="circle-title">A black circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000000"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
Updated 0.html. The page still shows the same centered black circle, with these changes:

- **No stray scrollbar.** Replaced the 100vw body width, which adds horizontal scroll when a vertical scrollbar exists, with a full-height html/body and hidden overflow.
- **Responsive sizing.** The SVG now caps at 400px but shrinks to fit small viewports instead of overflowing.
- **Accessibility.** Added a role, an accessible title inside the SVG, and a readable page title in place of the hash.
- **Explicit styling.** Set the circle fill and page background explicitly rather than relying on browser defaults, and added box-sizing to the reset.
